quiz.title: T1.3: Methods
quiz.description: Scenario-based questions on instance vs class methods, class parameters in methods (..#ParamName), method arguments and return types, passing objects to methods, pass by reference, multidimensional variables by reference, and ##super for superclass methods in InterSystems IRIS ObjectScript.

options: Only the Area instance method can access the PI class parameter using ..#PI; this syntax does not work in the FromDiameter class method.
The code body of Area can reference the Radius property using relative dot syntax, while this is not possible in the FromDiameter class method.
You need to create an instance of Sample.Circle to use the FromDiameter method but this is not necessary when calling the Area class method.
The FromDiameter class method can call the Area class method but Area can not call FromDiameter.
questions.explanation: Instance methods like Area() have access to the current object context and can reference properties using the .. (double-dot) syntax (e.g., ..Radius). Class methods like FromDiameter() have no object context and therefore cannot use .. to access instance properties. However, both instance and class methods CAN access class parameters using ..#ParamName (option A is incorrect). Class methods do not require an instance to call (option C is reversed). Instance methods can call class methods (option D is incorrect). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

questions.question:
An application provides utility methods that return tax information for a city. The tax rate may change occasionally.

Which of the following code blocks shows how this class can be implemented most efficiently?
questions.explanation: Option A is correct. Using a Parameter for the tax rate is the most efficient approach: parameters are class-level constants accessible via ..#TaxRate in both class and instance methods. Option B fails because ClassMethods cannot use .. to access properties (properties require an instance). Option C hardcodes the value in multiple places, making maintenance error-prone. Option D fails because ClassMethods cannot call instance methods via .. syntax (CurrentTaxRate is an instance method). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_parameters)

options: An error because class methods cannot call other class methods using .. syntax
questions.explanation: Class methods CAN call other class methods in the same class using the .. syntax. The Add() method calls ..Round(3.777777), and Round() uses $FN with the PRECISION parameter value of 4 to format the number to 4 decimal places, resulting in 3.7778. The ..# syntax accesses the parameter, and the .. syntax calls the class method -- both work from within a class method. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

questions.question:
Consider the following method signature.

ClassMethod ProcessData(ByRef data As %String, Output result As %String) As %Status

A developer calls it like this:

set myData = "input-value"
set myResult = "old-result"
set sc = ##class(App.Processor).ProcessData(.myData, .myResult)

Which of the following is true about myData and myResult when ProcessData begins executing?
options: Both myData and myResult retain their original values ("input-value" and "old-result")
myData retains "input-value" because it is ByRef; myResult is killed (undefined) because it is Output
Both are killed (undefined) because they are both passed by reference
myData is killed and myResult retains "old-result" because Output preserves existing values
questions.explanation: Both ByRef and Output are passed by reference, and neither keyword affects runtime behavior. The InterSystems documentation states: 'The ByRef and Output keywords provide information for the benefit of anyone using the InterSystems Class Reference. They do not affect the behavior of the code.' Both myData and myResult retain their original values when ProcessData begins executing. The Output keyword is a semantic hint indicating the parameter is intended to return a value, but it does NOT kill or clear the variable. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

options: An error because arrays cannot be passed to methods
Header followed by Body followed by Footer, each on a new line
Only "Header" because without ByRef only the first subscript is passed
An empty string because the lines variable has no top-level value
questions.explanation: Passing an array by reference (with the dot prefix .lines) sends the entire subscripted structure to the method. Inside BuildReport, the lines parameter has subscripts lines(1), lines(2), and lines(3) accessible. The $Order loop iterates through the subscripts in order, building a string with each line separated by $Char(10) (line feed). This is the standard pattern for passing multidimensional arrays to methods in ObjectScript. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

options: "Pending" because objects are passed by value (a copy is made)
"Active" because object references point to the same object in memory -- modifying properties through one reference is visible through all references
An error because objects must be passed with ByRef to allow modification
"Active" but only because the ByRef keyword is implied for objects
questions.explanation: In ObjectScript, when you pass an object to a method (even without ByRef), the object reference (oref) is passed by value. However, both the caller's variable and the method's parameter point to the same object in memory. Modifying the object's properties through either reference affects the same underlying object. ByRef would only be needed if the method wanted to reassign the caller's variable to a different object entirely. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

options: "Drawing generic shape"
"Circle with radius 5"
"Drawing generic shape -> Circle with radius 5"
An error because ##super() cannot be used in a method that returns a value
questions.explanation: ##super() calls the parent class's implementation of the same method. In App.Circle's Draw(), ##super() calls App.Shape's Draw() which returns "Drawing generic shape". That return value is stored in base, then concatenated with the circle-specific text. ##super() works with return values and can pass arguments just like any other method call. This is the standard pattern for extending parent behavior while adding subclass-specific logic. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods_override)

options: Result: 3
An error because Output parameters cannot be used with class methods
An empty string because .answer was not initialized before the call
questions.explanation: The Divide method receives a=10, b=3. Since b is not 0, it sets result (which is the caller's answer variable via Output) to 10/3 = 3.333333333333333333 and returns $$$OK. The caller checks $$$ISOK(sc) which is true, then writes the answer. Output parameters work with both class methods and instance methods. Note: the Output keyword is a semantic hint indicating the parameter returns a value; it does not affect runtime behavior (both ByRef and Output pass by reference identically). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

options: "Name is required"
"Age cannot be negative"
"Age exceeds maximum"
An error because ..ValidateAge() cannot be called from a ClassMethod
questions.explanation: ValidatePerson is called with name = "John" (not empty, passes first check) and age = -5. It then calls ..ValidateAge(-5). ClassMethods CAN call other ClassMethods using the .. syntax. ValidateAge checks -5 < 0 which is true, and returns an error status with "Age cannot be negative". This error is returned back through ValidatePerson, and GetErrorText displays the message. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_status)

options: An error because you cannot call Increment() without an argument
questions.explanation: The method signature includes a default value: amount As %Integer = 1. When called without arguments, amount defaults to 1. First call: 0+1=1, returns 1. Second call: 1+5=6, returns 6. Third call: 6+1=7, returns 7. The Value property persists across calls because the method modifies the instance state via ..Value. Default argument values allow flexible method signatures. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

options: hello world
HELLO WORLD
An error because class methods cannot modify ByRef arrays
An empty string because the array is killed by the ByRef keyword
questions.explanation: The array is passed by reference using the dot prefix (.items), which gives the Transform method access to all subscripts. The method iterates through each subscript using $Order and converts the values to uppercase using $ZCONVERT with the "U" flag. Since the array is passed by reference, the modifications to data(key) directly affect the caller's items array. The output is "HELLO WORLD". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

options: $$$OK because the base Validate() returns OK and the method stops there
An error status with "Email required"
An error status with "Invalid email" because ##super() returned OK, Email is not empty, but Email does not contain "@"
An error because ##super() cannot return a %Status value
questions.explanation: The execution flow is: App.Extended.Validate() calls ##super() which runs App.Base.Validate() returning $$$OK. Since sc is OK, execution continues. Email is "invalid-email" (not empty), so the first Email check passes. But "invalid-email" does not contain "@" (the [ operator checks for substring containment), so the method returns the "Invalid email" error. This demonstrates how ##super() enables layered validation. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods_override)

options: [APP] User logged in
[AUDIT] User logged in
An error because AuditLogger does not define its own Log() method
[APP][AUDIT] User logged in
questions.explanation: App.AuditLogger inherits the Log() method from App.Logger. When Log() is called on App.AuditLogger, the ..#LOGPREFIX reference resolves to the parameter value defined in App.AuditLogger, which is "AUDIT". Parameters can be overridden in subclasses, and ..# always resolves to the value in the class the method is being called on, not the class where the method was originally defined. This is a form of parametric polymorphism. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_parameters)

The %IsA() method checks whether an object is an instance of a specified class OR any of its subclasses. Passing a Sample.Patient instance would return true for %IsA("Sample.Person") because Patient extends Person. Option A fails because %ClassName() returns only the short class name ("Person") without the package, and it would reject valid subclass instances. Option C uses $CLASSNAME which is not a standard ObjectScript function. Option D uses %TypeOf() which does not exist. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_model_inheritance_extents)

questions.question:
Consider the following method.

ClassMethod GetStats(ByRef counts As %Integer) As %Status
{
  set counts("total") = 100
  set counts("active") = 75
  set counts("inactive") = 25
  return $$$OK
}

A developer calls:

set myCount = 0
set myCount("extra") = 999
set sc = ##class(App.Reports).GetStats(.myCount)
write myCount, !
write myCount("total"), !
write myCount("extra")

What is the output?
options: An error because ByRef kills the variable before the method starts

0
100
An <UNDEFINED> error because the method replaced the array
questions.explanation: With ByRef, the caller's variable (including all subscripts) is passed to the method intact. The method adds subscripts "total", "active", and "inactive" to the counts array but does not modify the top-level value or the existing "extra" subscript. After the call, myCount retains its top-level value of 0, myCount("total") is 100 (set by the method), and myCount("extra") is 999 (untouched by the method). Neither ByRef nor Output kills the variable -- both keywords are semantic hints that do not affect runtime behavior. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

options: An error because abstract methods cannot be called
"data from file"
"DATA FROM FILE"
An error because App.DataSource cannot be compiled with an abstract method
questions.explanation: The Process() method calls ..FetchData(). Since the actual object is an App.FileSource instance, its FetchData() implementation runs, returning "data from file". Process() then passes this through $ZCONVERT with "U" to convert to uppercase, resulting in "DATA FROM FILE". This demonstrates the Template Method design pattern: the base class defines the algorithm (Process) while subclasses provide specific implementations (FetchData). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

options: An error because you cannot concatenate $List values with _
questions.explanation: The method iterates through the arr subscripts (1, 2, 3) using $Order and builds a $List by concatenating $ListBuild values. $List concatenation with _ is valid and produces a longer $List. After processing all three elements, list contains $LB("Red", "Green", "Blue"), and $ListLength returns 3. The data array is passed ByRef and result is passed as Output; both keywords pass by reference and neither affects runtime behavior (they are semantic hints for documentation). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flistbuild)

options: Compilation succeeds and App.SpecialHandler.OnEvent returns "Special: Custom: Base handler: <event>"
A compile error occurs because App.CustomHandler.OnEvent is marked Final and cannot be overridden
Compilation succeeds but the Final keyword is ignored in subclasses
A runtime error occurs when OnEvent is called
questions.explanation: The [ Final ] keyword on App.CustomHandler.OnEvent() prevents any subclass from overriding that method. When App.SpecialHandler attempts to define its own OnEvent(), the compiler detects the violation and raises a compile-time error. Final methods are used to lock down critical behavior and prevent subclasses from changing it. This is enforced at compile time, not runtime. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods_override)
